Weekly Context & Takeaways

Week outcome: 4 winners, 16 losers, -$1,296.20 after $88.20 in commissions. Weekly profit factor 0.42 based on net winning and losing trade totals. Largest closed-trade equity drawdown within this reporting week: $1,296.20, measured from a zero starting point and prior intraperiod realized P&L peaks; this is not YTD or account-equity drawdown.

Where the edge performed: Tuesday was the strongest futures day at +$140.80. The two largest winners were the October 6 morning longs, +$328.40 and +$293.40 net.

What hurt: Wednesday (-$602.40) and Friday (-$602.80) were the largest losing days, each with zero winning trades. This aligns with the ongoing red-day / consecutive-loss research theme, but one week alone cannot establish a reliable filter.

Previous stop hunt: The earlier overnight trade stopped out before the subsequent downside move. Review its stop placement and the stop-hunt filter behavior as a separate observation; do not infer an alternate live fill from the screenshot.

DLL interruption: The later October 7 short was auto-liquidated by Tradovate at 3:06:31 AM ET due to the $600 account DLL. Actual net -$80.40. Matched research reached a +7R target around 7:31 AM ET. The distinction is account risk control versus strategy outcome, and +7R was not realized.

Management Research Status

Current research focus includes the +1R stop-to-−0.75R experiment, the +1.25R stop-hunt activation, failed winners and DLL interruptions. This report does not simulate the combined management rules or assert that a candidate trade would have survived the stop-hunt replay. No settings change is recommended from this week alone.

Risk Scaling & Interpretation

Actual contract quantities varied from one to four MNQ across the week. Net-dollar trade outcomes are not directly comparable to a fixed-risk backtest. The research-matched initial stop distances are shown under Research Details. A verified live initial-risk snapshot per trade is required to calculate precise live realized R or a live risk-tier contribution; the research stop distance must not be substituted without validation.
